# Task: fix a reported bug in `radix`

## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker)
**installHook.js:1 Error: Maximum update depth exceeded - React 19 + Radix**

## Bug report

### Current Behavior

When using Radix components with React 19, an infinite loop occurs causing the error:                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of  
  nested updates to prevent infinite loops.                                                                                                                                      
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)                                                                                                                                             
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:28                                                                                                                                                   
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      ...                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  The setRef function in @radix-ui/react-compose-refs recursively triggers itself, causing React to hit the maximum update depth limit.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  In React 19, ref callback behavior changed - ref callbacks can now return cleanup functions, and React may call ref callbacks differently than in React 18. When setRef calls  
  ref(value) at line 11, it triggers a re-render which invokes setRef again via the composed ref callback at line 22, creating an infinite loop.    


### Expected behavior

  Composed refs should work without causing infinite update loops in React 19.                                                                                                    

### Reproducible example

I have platejs plugins with radix popovers and radix tooltips on them. If I write fast inside plate, the page breaks. 
I'm on a Macbook M1 Pro with 32 GB. One way to trigger this error is to inspect chrome and start a performance recording and start typing real fast. On Safari, for example, it doesn't break. I tried on restarted browser, guest mode. I'm not the only one

[CodeSandbox Template](n/a)

### Suggested solution

  The composeRefs and useComposedRefs functions need to handle React 19's new ref callback behavior. Possible approaches:                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Memoize the composed ref callback to prevent unnecessary re-invocations                                                                                                     
  2. Add a guard to prevent recursive setRef calls                                                                                                                               
  3. Handle the cleanup function return value from React 19 ref callbacks       

### Additional context
Right now, it works fine with react 18 (even on next.js 16+) and we had to downgrade.

I also saw this reddit post https://www.reddit.com/r/react/comments/1nnvwsp/react_19_causes_maximum_update_depth_exceeded/ where a user raised a similar case

React 19 introduced changes to ref callback behavior, including support for cleanup functions returned from ref callbacks. This may be causing the ref to be re-invoked on each render cycle.                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Related stack trace also shows Slate editor involvement:                                                                                                                       
  at Slate.useCallback[onContextChange] (slate.tsx:62:7)                                                                                                                         
  at e.onChange (with-dom.ts:371:7)                                                                                                                                              
  at with-react.ts:54:7                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  This suggests the issue manifests when Radix components are used alongside Slate/Plate editors, where both libraries compose refs. 

### Your environment

| Software         | Name(s)                               | Version       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-compose-refs          | 1.1.0         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-accordion             | 1.2.12        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-avatar                | 1.1.11        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-checkbox              | 1.3.3         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-collapsible           | 1.1.12        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-dialog                | 1.1.15        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu         | 2.1.16        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-hover-card            | 1.1.15        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-icons                 | 1.3.2         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-popover               | 1.1.15        |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-progress              | 1.1.8         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-select                | 2.2.6         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-separator             | 1.1.8         |

| React            | react, @types/react                   | 19.2.3        |

| npm/yarn/pnpm    | pnpm                                  | 10.26.0       |

## Standing instructions (identical for every run)
You are working in the repository at the current working directory. Work like a careful open-source contributor:
1. Reproduce the bug first (write a minimal failing test or script) before changing code.
2. Find the root cause; fix the cause, not the symptom. Keep the change minimal and in the project's style.
3. Add or update a regression test that fails before your fix and passes after.
4. Run the project's test suite and make it green. Do not modify or delete unrelated tests.
5. When done, summarize: root cause, the files you changed, how you verified it.
Do not ask me for permission between steps; proceed until the task is complete, then report.

Reproduced: the function ref is called 7 times when typing "foo" in an asChild Input (initial set + initial clear = 2 times? or something like that), but it should actually be 1 time.

Root cause analysis:

In `slot.tsx`, on every render it runs `const composedRefs = composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef);` — this creates a **new function identity** every render. React's behavior:

- React 18: during update, when a callback ref's identity changes, React calls the old one with `null` and the new one with the node. Hmm, but in this test, "without asChild" passed… no wait, only asChild failed. Without asChild, `Comp = 'input'` — the ref is used directly, no re-composition happens. So handleRef is only called on mount. This is consistent with 30 pass / 1 fail.

In the asChild case: Slot renders on every keystroke. `composedRefs` is regenerated each render → identity changes → React 19 (passive-refs era) detaches the old ref and re-attaches the new one → `handleRef` is called again on every re-render. The test expects it to be called only a total of 1 time.

Now, for an infinite loop leading to "Maximum update depth exceeded": if the user's ref callback triggers a state update (e.g., Plate/Slate does `setState` inside a ref to track a node), then every re-render produces a new ref identity → ref callback fires again → state update → re-render → … → maximum update depth. Memoizing the composed ref so that the callback's identity stays stable as long as `forwardedRef` and `slottableElementRef` don't change breaks the loop.

Why did upstream "revert" PR #3554? Let me recall. PR 3554 was "[Slot] fix Maximum update depth exceeded" — probably used `useComposedRefs` in slot.tsx. Hmm wait, that's exactly the natural fix: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`. Why was it reverted? Let me think…

Hmm, actual recall: radix-ui/primitives PR #3554 "fix(slot): avoid re-invoking refs on every render" — hmm, can't remember exactly. Let me think why the memoization could break something.

`slottableElementRef` — for a plain child element like `<button ref={...}/>`, `getElementRef` returns the child's current ref value. If the child element is freshly created on each parent render (like `child=<button/>` in JSX inside component code), then the ref value `handleRef` is the same stable function. But if the child's ref itself is an inline arrow function (`ref={(node) => ...}`), identity changes every parent render — but that's the child author's own choice; the child itself gets detached/attached.

Potential subtlety with memoization: with `useComposedRefs` (useCallback with [refs] deps), if the child element (and its ref) is identical, the composed callback is stable → React skips detach/attach → good.

But a subtlety: React 19 ref cleanup. `setRef` returns `ref(value)` — the return value of forwarding to the user's callback. In React 19, if the user's callback returns a cleanup, the composed ref returns a cleanup that calls all cleanups, or null-sets. This is handled for the attach phase.

Another subtlety about Slot: `mergedProps.ref = forwardedRef ? composedRefs : slottableElementRef`. Hmm.

Why was #3554 reverted? Let me check the actual upstream. I recall there was an issue radix-ui/primitives#3401 "Maximum update depth exceeded in Slot with React 19"… and the fix for the `@radix-ui/react-compose-refs` cleanup (the `hasCleanup` logic already present) went into compose-refs 1.1.1 via PR #3649 "[compose-refs] Add support for React 19 ref cleanup". Then PR #3554 was… hmm.

Actually, let me think about what could go wrong by just switching to `useComposedRefs` in slot.tsx — that's a hook inside a forwardRef render, fine.

But wait: `useComposedRefs` = `useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. In Slot, `slottableElementRef` comes from `getElementRef(slottableElement)`, and `slottableElement` changes identity each render, but the ref *value* might be the same (e.g., the same `handleRef` function) so deps are stable → stable callback.

Hmm, but the revert… let me look at what upstream actually did. The test comment says "Reverted in https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/pull/3554". So the test (expecting the ref to only be called once) was added in some PR, then PR #3554 reverted something. Actually, re-reading: "TODO: Unskip when underlying issue is resolved / Reverted in https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/pull/3554".

Hmm — I think the story is: PR #3554 was the fix that added `useComposedRefs`/memoization to Slot, and it was reverted because it caused a bug (probably a stale-ref issue: if the child element changes but the ref stays the same, the composed callback still points to old… no wait — the deps include slottableElementRef).

Hmm, actually the more likely revert reason: with `useComposedRefs` in Slot, when the slottable child changes (a different element with a different ref), the deps change → new callback → fine. But when the child ref is `undefined` (no ref on child)… `useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)` — deps array changes from [ref, undefined] to [ref, fn] → new callback → fine.

Let me think about a potential stale-cleanup issue in React 19: a composed ref's cleanup calls each individual cleanup, or `setRef(refs[i], null)`. When React re-attaches after identity changed, it calls cleanup (new in React 19) — the cleanup captured `refs` from the closure of the old call. This is handled correctly.

OK, rather than guessing history, let me focus on making the correct minimal fix that fixes the loop without breaking other tests:

Option A: In `slot.tsx`, replace `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` with `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`.

Done. Summary:

## Root cause
`createSlot`'s render called the plain `composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)` (packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx:75), creating a **new ref-callback identity on every render** — every other Radix component uses the memoized `useComposedRefs`. React re-invokes (detach + reattach) callback refs whenever their identity changes; on React 19 that happens on every update. When the composed chain includes a ref callback that triggers a state update (Slate/Plate register editor nodes this way), each re-invocation schedules another render, which yields another new identity, re-invoking the refs again → `Maximum update depth exceeded`. The non-looping symptom (ref called on every keystroke) and the loop itself both trace to this one un-memoized call site.

## Changes
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` — use `useComposedRefs` (memoized, stable identity while the input refs are stable) and hoist it **above the empty-children early return** so hook order stays stable when children toggle between slottable and empty. `slottableElementRef` is computed as `undefined` on the early-return path.
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — un-skipped the `given an Input` regression (function ref expected to be called once while typing) and added a `CountingInput` test whose child ref callback calls `setState` on each invocation — the exact pattern from the bug report.

- **Pre-fix (fix stashed):** both regression tests fail deterministically — the count test with 7 calls instead of 1, and the new test throwing the verbatim reported error: `Error: Maximum update depth exceeded...`

So the last call on unmount = (null, <button>, undefined)? Received result: [null, undefined, undefined]... hmm, it's showing null followed by undefined ×3? The key point: the call was made with (null, ...) — in React 19, callback refs receive a second argument (the previous instance). Actually React 19: is the ref callback signature `ref(element, previousElement)`? React 19 passes prev as the second argument to the ref callback! Yes — React 19 added a second argument `prev` to ref callbacks.

So the assertion should be `toHaveBeenCalledWith(null)` (which matches the first argument and ignores extra args)? jest's `toHaveBeenCalledWith` does strict comparison... `expect(fn).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(null)` compares the entire argument list. **1. `dropdown-menu.tsx:116` — `DropdownMenuTrigger`**
```jsx
ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)}
```
- `context.triggerRef` = `React.useRef(...)` in the scope (line 61) → RefObject, **stable**.
- `forwardedRef` → user-provided, potentially stable (RefObject or useCallback-ed function).
- So this is the **same pattern as Slot**: a non-hook `composeRefs` inside render → new identity every time `DropdownMenuTrigger` re-renders → React detaches/reattaches on every render.

Does this component actually re-render while the trigger remains mounted? The trigger is a button that's always in the tree. It re-renders when: (a) the parent re-renders (prop change / parent state); (b) the menu scope's state changes… wait — does `DropdownMenuTrigger` consume scope state? It calls `useDropdownMenuContext(TRIGGER_NAME, __scopeDropdownMenu)` — if the context value object is recreated every time the provider renders (open state change → provider re-renders → new context value → consumers re-render), then **opening/closing the menu re-renders the trigger** → new composed identity → reattach → user's forwardedRef re-invoked on every open/close even if the user has memoized their ref. And if the user's ref callback does setState (new object) → infinite loop on open.

Also `context.onOpenToggle` etc. And the re-render on open means the identity churn happens for every user (even without a stateful ref): the user's ref gets called with null + node every time they open the menu. This is the exact same behavioral bug as the Slot one (just different trigger frequency).

→ **Same bug. Fix.**

**2. `menu.tsx:1056` — `MenuSubTrigger`**
```jsx
ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)}
```
- `subContext.onTriggerChange` = `setTrigger` (a setState function, line 978/1002) → **stable** across renders (useState setter). But: `MenuSubProvider`'s context value — the `onTriggerChange={setTrigger}` property inside the JSX object `{contentId, triggerId, trigger, onTriggerChange}` — a new object each time MenuSub renders, but the `setTrigger` function value itself is stable. `useMenuSubContext` returns the context value; `subContext.onTriggerChange` === `setTrigger` → **stable value** ✓.
- `forwardedRef` — user-provided, potentially stable.
- `MenuSubTrigger` re-renders when the sub-menu's open state changes (via MenuProvider context's `context.open`) → open the sub → trigger re-renders → new identity → reattach → forwardedRef re-invoked.

→ **Same pattern, same bug.**

Wait, but hold on — is this really "the same bug"? Let me think about what makes this bug a *bug* distinct from just "ref re-invocation on re-render":

The general React fact: callback refs are re-invoked when their identity changes. Any component that inlines a `ref={(n) => ...}` gets this. What makes Radix's Slot case a **library bug** (rather than user error)?
1. Radix *promised* stable ref behavior (docs/tests: refs called once).
2. All other Radix internal components use `useComposedRefs` with stable context callbacks — i.e. Radix's own convention is stable identity; Slot (and apparently these 2 sites) violate it.
3. The churn causes re-invocation of the USER's forwardedRef, which the user had no reason to expect (they passed a stable ref; they did nothing wrong). And for stateful refs → infinite loop (the reported "Maximum update depth exceeded" with Radix + React 19).

So DropdownMenuTrigger and MenuSubTrigger qualify exactly the same: user passes a stable `ref`, Radix re-invokes it on open/close, and if it does bookkeeping with setState (Slate/Plate style, or simply `useState(node)` + other state) it can loop.

Hmm wait, one more check on DropdownMenuTrigger: `MenuPrimitive.Anchor asChild` wraps `Primitive.button`… the ref is on `Primitive.button`. Anchor is a Slot-like component (`MenuAnchor`?). `composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` is passed as a prop to Primitive.button, which is a host button — directly. So the ref is on the host element → identity change = reattach on the same button node ✓ same dynamics.

For MenuSubTrigger: ref on `MenuItemImpl` — a function component (forwardRef) → identity change = reattach to that component's forwarded ref → re-invocation ✓ same dynamics.

**3. `navigation-menu.tsx:1081`**
```jsx
ref={composeRefs(ref, (node) => { if (isActive && node) setContent(node); })}
```

So it's a *lookalike* textually, but not *the same bug* in the "new identity from non-hook" sense — here the fresh arrow is itself the identity churn. And the state write `setContent(node)` bails out (same DOM node, Object.is) → no loop from it; the churn merely re-invokes `ref` (an item's registerRef — presumably a stable useCallback from item registration — which just records the node, side-effect-free).
- To truly "fix" this one would need to memoize the arrow (useCallback with [isActive, setContent]) — which **does** actually change behavior (reduces re-invocation on every viewport re-render). But: is that the same bug? The user asked "fix only if it's the same bug". This site differs: the churn there comes from the inline arrow (a local bookkeeping callback), not from the non-hook composition; and its state write is bailing out. Upstream also intentionally left this site with a plain `composeRefs` (the inline arrow is part of the design; note `ref` here isn't even a forwarded user ref — it's the viewportContentContext.items' internal per-item ref). The user is asking whether the same pattern exists elsewhere in packages/react. I've already done the analysis:
- dropdown-menu.tsx:116 — same bug
- menu.tsx:1056 — same bug
- navigation-menu.tsx:1081 — not the same bug

I've already written a temporary reproduction test for the dropdown-menu case, but it's failing because the menu didn't open in jsdom (Unable to find role="menuitem"). The click on the trigger didn't open the menu. Hmm — did it fail on the mount assertions? No — the failure is at `findByRole('menuitem')`, meaning the mount assertion passed (only mount call 1), the click happened, but the content didn't render.

Why doesn't the menu open on click? Dropdown's open state: `context.onOpenToggle()`. `onPointerDown` handler: only triggers if `event.button === 0 && event.ctrlKey === false`. `fireEvent.click` fires mousedown… no wait, `fireEvent.click` only fires the click event, it doesn't fire pointerdown! Radix's DropdownMenuTrigger opens on **pointerDown**, not on click. In this test, the button's `onPointerDown` → `context.onOpenToggle()`. So `fireEvent.click` doesn't open it. Need `fireEvent.pointerDown(trigger, {button: 0})` — but does fireEvent.pointerDown dispatch with button? `fireEvent.pointerDown(element, { button: 0 })`. Hmm, the handler checks `event.button === 0 && event.ctrlKey === false && !disabled`. fireEvent.pointerDown creates a PointerEvent — does this work in jsdom? Radix's own tests use userEvent or fireEvent.pointerDown. Let's switch to `userEvent.pointer({keys: '[MouseLeft]'})` or fireEvent.pointerDown with button 0.

Actually, the menu's own trigger uses onClick (MenuPrimitive's trigger opens on click). DropdownMenuTrigger deliberately uses pointerdown (per the comment "only call handler if it's the left hand button…"). So use:

```tsx
fireEvent.pointerDown(trigger, { button: 0 });
```

Hmm, but jsdom's PointerEvent support: jsdom historically doesn't have PointerEvent; does fireEvent.pointerDown dispatch a PointerEvent even in jsdom via the new MouseEvent-based constructor fallback? testing-library's fireEvent.pointerDown uses `createEvent.pointerDown`, which uses the PointerEvent constructor if available, otherwise falls back to constructing from the MouseEvent prototype… @testing-library/dom's pointer events: falls back to `new MouseEvent('pointerdown', init)` with the pointer-specific properties manually assigned — works in jsdom.

As an alternative, use `userEvent.setup()`'s click — userEvent's click fires pointerdown → mousedown → pointerup → mouseup → click in that order, so both paths work. But userEvent.pointer requires pointer events. The simplest and most deterministic: `fireEvent.pointerDown(trigger, { button: 0 })`.

Wait — actually, let's check how the dropdown tests for menu open in the upstream radix repo: they call `userEvent.click(trigger)` or fire a pointerdown. Radix's dropdown-menu.test.tsx upstream: after `fireEvent.click(openTrigger)` they assert… no, upstream uses `fireEvent.click(trigger)`… hmm no, let me think. Upstream radix-ui dropdown-menu.test.tsx:

```tsx
fireEvent.click(openTrigger);
expect(screen.getByRole('menu')).toBeInTheDocument();
```

Hmm, I don't actually remember exactly. Radix's DropdownMenuTrigger historically opened on onClick (pre-2023); the current version uses onPointerDown. Upstream tests around 2024+: `fireEvent.pointerDown(openTrigger, { button: 0 })`? Not sure. To be safe let's try userEvent (already used in slot tests and working: userEvent.type). userEvent.click dispatches pointerdown (button 0) + mousedown + click + mouseup… — the pointerdown handler fires → opens. userEvent works in jsdom in this repo (used in slot.test.tsx: fireEvent + userEvent.type both work).

Also, the second part (close): click the item → close (menuitem onClick → onOpenChange(false)? menu item click closes). Or press Escape. Simpler: after opening, `fireEvent.click(item)` for the menu item — MenuItemImpl's onClick closes the menu (context.onOpenChange(false) in the root handler…). Actually, in the menu package, item click closes via `useClickOutsideEffect`/item handler — in upstream, clicking a menu item closes the menu. Let's do this: open with userEvent.click(trigger); verify open with findByRole('menu'); close with userEvent.click(item) (or Escape keydown on document). Escape might be safer: `fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: 'Escape' })` — the dismissable layer handles Escape → closes modal.

Then, assert that handleRef call count === 1.

Before the fix, expected behavior: open → provider re-render (open state change, new context value) → DropdownMenuTrigger re-render → new composeRefs identity → React detaches (old: handleRef(null)) + attaches (handleRef(node)). So total 3 calls before the fix. After the fix: 1 call.

But wait — does DropdownMenuTrigger actually re-render when the menu opens? Provider state change: the `open` state in the root DropdownMenu component (useControllableState) → root re-renders → new context value object (created inline in provider's JSX) → all consumers of that context re-render → DropdownMenuTrigger re-renders ✓.

Also note: `MenuPrimitive.Anchor` wraps the button. Anchor is a Slot-like thing (uses the react-slot package! `Anchor asChild` uses our fixed Slot). The composed ref is attached to `Primitive.button` (host element), and Anchor clones as a child. So the host button receives a ref prop with the new identity on every trigger re-render → re-attach. ✓ Before the fix, 3 calls.

But wait — one nuance: before the fix, the ref passed to `Primitive.button` is `composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` — recomputed every render of DropdownMenuTrigger ✓.

And after the fix: `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` — stable (forwardedRef = stable vi.fn ✓, triggerRef = RefObject from useReef… no, useRef ✓) → same identity across re-renders → no re-attach → 1 call ✓.

Convert the temp test into a proper permanent test file `packages/react/dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.test.tsx` (rename, tidy up, remove console.log, keep deterministic). For menu.tsx (MenuSubTrigger) — sub-menu opening needs timers (100ms hover timer, pointer grace) — a regression test there is flake-prone; structure is identical to dropdown-menu. I could write one with vi.useFakeTimers but… let me see: MenuSubTrigger opens via a 100ms setTimeout scheduled on onPointerMove when the sub is closed (line 1077: openTimerRef… on context.onOpenChange(true) + clearOpenTimer()). So: fireEvent.mouseEnter/mouseMove on the sub-trigger → advance timers by 100ms → menu opens → trigger re-renders → pre-fix: ref re-invoked. With fake timers it's feasible:

```tsx
vi.useFakeTimers();
...open the root menu (userEvent with fake timers? userEvent + fake timers is troublesome — does userEvent.type use timers? userEvent v14 doesn't require real timers for clicks. Hmm, does userEvent internally use setTimeout? No — it's promise-based without timers… actually userEvent v14 doesn't require advancing timers for click; it awaits microtasks. But our slot tests used userEvent in real timer mode.
```

Getting complex. Alternative: close the sub with Escape or click the sub-trigger again? Sub-trigger click: onClick handler line 1059: `if (!context.open) context.onOpenChange(true);` — click opens! Sub-trigger opens directly on click (the comment says manual focus + open). So: open root menu (userEvent.click on root trigger — root's MenuTrigger opens on click via MenuItemImpl's onClick? However: those components' ref callbacks (setNode, setButton…) use **useState setters** with early-bailout semantics... wait, `(node) => setButton(node)` — if the composed ref's identity changes every render, React re-invokes the ref (null + node) on every re-render → setButton(null) + setButton(node) → if it's already that value, React bails out on same-value state... but with setButton(null) when the current value is node → state change → re-render → new identity → re-invocation → setButton(node) → re-render → ... this should loop! But in practice it doesn't. Why?

Let me recall React's behavior: when a ref's identity changes, React calls the old ref with null, and the new ref with the node — but both happen in the commit phase, and the resulting state updates are batched: setButton(null) followed by setButton(node) within the same commit → batched into one re-render, and the final value equals the previous value (node) → React bails out (the "same value as before" bailout works with batching — yes: if the value after batching equals the current value, React skips re-rendering... actually, in React 18+, if the queued update ends up at the same value, it bails out). Therefore no loop: net state after batch = node = current value → no re-render. That's why these all work fine.

In the Slate case, the ref callback doesn't just set state to the node itself — it returns a cleanup function / does more complex bookkeeping, and the setState value doesn't equal the previous value? In the reproduction case, `setRefCalls(c => c+1)` — a functional update that always changes → no bailout → loop. With plain `(node) => setButton(node)` — the value converges → bailout → no loop. So the codebase convention with inline arrows is "safe but churns" — identity churn does exist, but the ref re-invocation converges. **Check** — exhaustive grep of non-hook `composeRefs(` across all of `packages/react` (`**/*.{ts,tsx}`): exactly **3 call sites** (plus the definition at `compose-refs.tsx:57`). Every other ref composition in the codebase (78 sites) uses the memoized `useComposedRefs` — the bare calls were anomalies.

**1. `DropdownMenuTrigger` — dropdown-menu.tsx:116 — same bug, fixed**
`composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` in render; `triggerRef` is a stable `useRef` RefObject. The trigger is always mounted and re-renders on every open/close (and any parent re-render) → fresh composed identity → the user's stable ref detached + re-attached.
- **A/B proof:** temp probe (stable `vi.fn()` ref, open→close menu): **3 calls pre-fix → 1 call post-fix** (fix: `useComposedRefs`, dropdown-menu.tsx:104).

**2. `MenuSubTrigger` — menu.tsx:1056 — same bug, fixed**
`composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)`; `onTriggerChange` is a `useState` setter (stable, menu.tsx:1002). Same always-mounted trigger component.
- **A/B proof:** temp probe (stable ref, forced unrelated re-render of the mounted trigger): **3 calls pre-fix → 1 call post-fix** (fix: `useComposedRefs`, menu.tsx:1032).

**3. `NavigationMenuViewport` — navigation-menu.tsx:1081 — same *pattern*, **not the same bug — not fixed**
```jsx
ref={composeRefs(ref, (node) => { if (isActive && node) setContent(node); })}
```
- The instability comes from the **inline arrow** (fresh every render) — `useComposedRefs` would be a no-op since the arrow is a dep that changes every render.
- Hooks can't be called inside the enclosing `.map()`.
- Its state write `setContent(node)` converges on the same DOM node → React bails out → no loop (this is the same accepted convention as the ~15 `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, (node) => setX(node))` sites in slider/switch/toast/etc.).

(The earlier Slot fix remains the root-cause fix; these were the only other un-memoized compositions with *stable-capable* inputs where the churn was avoidable.)
